newsitem.title: CHINA: China executes "homicide maniac", eight others.
newsitem.headline: China executes "homicide maniac", eight others.

text.p: China said on Saturday it had executed a man known as the "homicide maniac" and eight accomplices for the murders of 17 people, including a New Zealander, in the last two years.

From October 1994 to August 1996, Zhang Zhicheng and a dozen accomplices from central Hunan province carried out a series of armed robberies and murders in the southern city of Guangzhou and in the Pearl River Delta that borders Hong Kong, the official Xinhua news agency said.

On Saturday a Guangdong provincial court upheld death sentences against Zhang and his gang for killing 17 people and injuring five, it said. Sentence was carried out immediately after the verdict. Executions in China are carried out with a single bullet in the heart or back of the head.
Zhang's gang committed a total of 31 armed robberies, making off with 1.36 million yuan ($160,000) in cash and valuables, the court said.
"The New Zealander was killed in a bus and in broad daylight during one of their armed robberies," the court said. It did not further identify the New Zealander.
Gang leader Zhang was captured in a raid on a house in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen on November 16 after a manhunt of several months, Xinhua said.
Apart from those ordered executed, the court sentenced one man to death with a two-year reprieve, another to life in jail and two to terms of 18 years and 15 years, Xinhua said.
Zhang pleaded guilty and did not appeal. The rest of his gang appealed, Xinhua said.

China executed several thousand people last year in a nationwide crackdown on crime amid a surge in violent offences as reforms to liberalise the economy offered new opportunities for crime while widening the gap between rich and poor.
